title: Maine AI Laws

reading.body:
Maine's three AI laws are narrow: campaign ad disclosure, chatbot disclosure, and a study of artist copyright. None regulates compute, data centers, or power.

The pattern is disclosure and study rather than infrastructure control. LD1727 requires a business to tell a consumer when a chatbot may be mistaken for a human, enforced through the state's unfair trade practices law. LD517 requires a warning label on synthetic media in campaign ads that already carry a disclosure, with penalties tied to the ad spend. LD109 funds a $25,000 consultant to study how federal and national efforts protect artists from AI copyright infringement, with a report due December 3, 2025.

For AI specifically, these laws govern what users are told, not what systems are built or where they run. Nothing here touches siting, interconnection, electricity procurement, or the physical constraints that determine how much compute a state can host. A reader looking for Maine's position on data center load or grid capacity will not find it in this set.

What the data does not cover is equally clear. It lists three enacted laws and no pending bills, no agency rules, and no local ordinances. The chatbot and synthetic media provisions are the only ones with operative requirements, and both are disclosure duties. The copyright item is a study resolve, so it produces a report rather than an obligation.

body_html:
Maine has enacted 3 AI-related laws. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Maine

3 laws this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • LD517: An Act Regarding Synthetic Media in Campaign Advertising passed 2026-03-19

    This law requires public communications in Maine campaign advertising that already require a disclosure and contain synthetic media to include a specific warning that the audio, video and/or images have been manipulated or altered. It defines synthetic media, exempts satire, parody and certain clarity modifications, and limits broadcaster and newspaper liability to cases of actual knowledge. Violations can lead to civil penalties up to 500% of the expenditure and injunctive relief by the Attorney General.

  • LD109: Resolve, Directing the Maine Arts Commission to Study Federal and National Efforts to Protect Artists from Copyright Infringement by Artificial Intelligence Companies and Users and to Monitor Educational Use passed 2025-06-25

    Directs the Maine Arts Commission to study federal and national efforts to protect artists from copyright infringement by businesses and others promoting, creating, disseminating or using artificial intelligence software applications, and to study federal and national efforts to monitor educational use of copyrighted work. The commission must report findings and any suggested legislation to the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs by December 3, 2025. The resolve provides one time funding of $25,000 for a consultant and allows the commission to accept outside funding.

  • LD1727: An Act to Ensure Transparency in Consumer Transactions Involving Artificial Intelligence passed 2025-06-10

    This law requires a person using an artificial intelligence chatbot or other computer technology to engage in trade and commerce with a consumer to notify the consumer in a clear and conspicuous manner that the consumer is not engaging with a human being, if the use may mislead or deceive a reasonable consumer into believing otherwise. A violation is treated as a violation of the Maine Unfair Trade Practices Act.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Maine. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
